samples.summary: Copy buffer now survives every paste, so a later unrelated paste with identical clipboard text is silently treated as an internal paste
samples.evidence: Both view paste handlers dropped `this.sheet.clearCopyBuffer()` (worksheet.ts ~4941-4947, spreadsheet.ts ~724-728). `Sheet.paste` only clears the buffer for a cut (sheet.ts:2286). The internal-paste branch is selected purely by `text === this.copyBuffer.text` (sheet.ts:2243). After a copy-paste the buffer lives on indefinitely, so if the user later copies identical text from another application (or the same short value, e.g. "10"), the paste takes the internal path: it relocates formulas, replays the buffer's `rangeStyles`, and now also re-creates the buffer's merged blocks at the destination — none of which the foreign clipboard asked for. Previously the buffer was dropped after the first paste and any subsequent paste fell through to the external TSV path. The same widened window applies to a buffer that has gone stale through an intervening row/column insert: `copyBuffer.sourceRange` is never adjusted (no other code touches `copyBuffer`, per grep), so the relocation delta is computed from a position that no longer exists.

samples.summary: The new no-straddle-freeze-boundary invariant is not enforced on `setFreezePane`, so the guard added to paste and drag-move can be bypassed
samples.evidence: `planPasteMerges` (sheet.ts:2429-2433) and `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2685-2695) now refuse operations that would place a merged block across a freeze boundary, on the stated grounds that the renderer "paints a frozen pane and the scrolling body from a single block, so a straddling one is not drawable". But `setFreezePane(frozenRows, frozenCols)` at sheet.ts:514-518 just assigns `this.frozenRows`/`this.frozenCols` and persists them — it never inspects `this.merges`. Freezing 2 rows while a block spans rows 2-3 produces exactly the state the new refusals exist to prevent, reached in normal use (the freeze menu), not through a programmatic back door.

samples.summary: External (TSV/HTML) paste still writes into merge-covered cells, breaking the "covered cells hold no content" invariant the new merge code relies on
samples.evidence: `clearCellsUnderMerge` (sheet.ts:2557-2562) documents and depends on the invariant that covered cells hold no content, "otherwise they stay hidden under the merge and reappear when it is removed". The external branches (`html2grid(html, destStart)` at 2290, `string2grid(destStart, text)` at 2294) feed straight into `setGrid` -> `store.setGrid`, which writes raw srefs without `normalizeRefToAnchor` (sheet.ts:992-994), and `planPasteMerges`/`applyPasteMerges` are skipped entirely for external pastes (pastedMerges/replacedMerges stay empty). Pasting e.g. "1\t2\t3" at A3 while B3:C3 is merged writes a value into covered C3; it is invisible until the block is unmerged, at which point stale data resurfaces. The new `destStart = normalizeRefToAnchor(activeCell)` (line 2241) shifts external paste origins onto merge anchors, which makes multi-cell external pastes land on covered cells more often than before. The new test at merge.test.ts:681 only pastes two cells, so it lands on the anchor and does not exercise this.

samples.summary: `planPasteMerges` does not bound the pasted block against the sheet dimension, so a paste near the edge can create a merge outside the grid
samples.evidence: `pasted` is built by translating the recorded anchors (sheet.ts:2420-2423) and is only checked against the freeze boundary and destination overlap; nothing compares `anchor.r + span.rs - 1` / `anchor.c + span.cs - 1` against `this.dimension.rows`/`.columns` (which the rest of the file consults at e.g. 3446, 3459, 5378). Copying a block that ends on the last row and pasting it one row lower persists a merge whose covered srefs lie outside the addressable grid, which `rebuildMergeCoverMap` and the renderer then carry. `moveRangeTo` has the same gap, so this is parity rather than a regression, but the new paste path adds another way to reach it.

samples.summary: `selectPastedRange` under-selects a paste that carried merged blocks, because the grid omits covered cells
samples.evidence: `selectPastedRange` derives the selection from `rangeOf(grid)` (sheet.ts:2612-2626), and the pasted grid contains only cells with content — a merged block's covered cells are empty by invariant, exactly as the new `planPasteMerges` doc comment notes ("a merged block's covered cells hold nothing, so the grid omits them and its box is smaller than the block being reproduced"). After pasting a single merged block the bounding box collapses to the anchor and the code takes the `selectStart(from)` single-cell branch, so the selection no longer covers the region the user pasted. The translated destination range (already computed in `planPasteMerges`) would be the accurate selection.

mergedFrom.summary: `setFreezePane` accepts any freeze position without checking existing merged blocks, retroactively splitting a block across the boundary the new paste guard protects

finding.summary: `moveRangeTo` re-creates moved merged blocks at the destination without the new freeze-boundary check, so drag-move can create the very block `planPasteMerges` now refuses
finding.evidence: The delta adds `crossesFreezePane` and refuses an internal paste whose block would land across a frozen row/column (sheet.ts:2420-2424), justified as "the rule `canMergeSelection` enforces ... and the one the renderer assumes when it paints a frozen pane and the scrolling body from a single block". `moveRangeTo` has the sibling pre-flight checks (`merge-source-split` at 2659, `merge-dest-partial` at 2667) but no freeze check, and at 2749-2755 it unconditionally does `setMerge({r: anchor.r + deltaRow, c: anchor.c + deltaCol}, merge.span)`. Dragging a merged block from below a frozen row so it straddles the boundary therefore produces the exact invariant violation the paste guard was added for, on a normal user gesture.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing freeze check is present in `moveRangeTo`. At sheet.ts:2685-2695, after the `merge-source-split` (2668) and `merge-dest-partial` (2676) pre-flights and before any mutation, the method calls `this.crossesFreezePane(...)` on each moved merge's range translated by `deltaRow`/`deltaCol`, and on a hit calls `this.refuse('merge-move-frozen')` and returns. That return precedes `this.store.beginBatch()` (2712) and the `await this.store.setMerge(anchor, merge.span)` at 2774-2780 the finding points to, so the drag-move cannot create a block straddling a frozen row/column. The refusal is fully wired, not dead code: the union member is declared at sheet.ts:233, the view renders a message for it at view/worksheet.ts:114, it is documented at docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:112, and a test asserts it fires at test/sheet/merge.test.ts:712. The reviewer's quoted line numbers are offset by ~8-25 lines from the current working tree, consistent with reading a stale revision.

mergedFrom.summary: External (TSV/HTML) pastes still write into cells covered by a destination merge, hiding the pasted values

finding.summary: Single-cell-destination exemption rests on a premise that selectRow/selectColumn/selectAllCells break, so a single-cell internal paste can still write into a hidden covered cell
finding.evidence: `planPasteMerges` returns `{pasted, replaced: []}` whenever `isCollapsedRange(destRange)` (sheet.ts:2424), justified by the comment "every path that sets `activeCell` normalizes it with `normalizeRefToAnchor`". That is false: `selectRow` sets `this.activeCell = { r: row, c: 1 }` (sheet.ts:3367), `selectColumn` sets `{ r: 1, c: col }` (sheet.ts:3380) and `selectAllCells` sets `{ r: 1, c: 1 }` (sheet.ts:3421) — none normalize. With a merge covering e.g. A2:A4 (anchor A2), clicking the row-3 header and pasting a single copied cell gives activeCell = A3 (a covered cell); the collapsed-destRange branch skips all merge handling and `setGrid` writes the value straight into A3, where it is invisible under the block and resurfaces only on unmerge. The multi-cell variant is refused by the split check, so only the single-cell path leaks.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise is factually wrong about the repository. The exemption comment at sheet.ts:2447-2450 does not claim "every path that sets activeCell normalizes it"; it says `paste` normalizes its start — and it does: sheet.ts:2241 computes `const destStart = this.normalizeRefToAnchor(this.activeCell);`, with the comment at 2235-2240 explicitly naming selectRow/selectColumn/selectAllCells as the non-normalizing setters that motivate the normalization. `normalizeRefToAnchor` (844-846) maps covered srefs to the anchor via `mergeCoverMap` (838). The relocated grid and the paste delta are both derived from `destStart` (2245-2251), so for a single-cell internal paste destRange[0] == destStart == the merge anchor, and `setGrid` writes to A2, never the covered A3. The exact scenario the finding describes (merge A2:A4, `selectRow(3)`, paste one copied cell, then unmerge) is asserted by an existing test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:748-773, which checks A2 holds the pasted value and A3 is empty after unmerge. The covered-cell write path is therefore already guarded and unreachable.
